free_tier.stated: A rolling grant and fellowship programme running since 2018 with no published range. The operator's own words, quoted: 'We encourage you to think big, but we also will consider very small grants if they might change the trajectory of your life. We encourage applications from all ages and all parts of the world.' On the amount: 'There is NO typical grant range or average award amount - funding is project specific.' On credentials: 'We probably don't care much about your formal education, credentials, or awards, unless they're particularly germane to who you are or your idea.' The only stated eligibility bar is age: 'To be eligible for an EV grant, all applicants must be 13 years of age or older.' The route is a 1,500-word proposal through a form, with dedicated lanes for India, Africa and the Caribbean, and Ukraine. One condition applies to how the text is produced: 'Emergent Ventures no longer accepts AI-written applications. We will test all submissions and reject those using AI for anything other than proofreading.'

One page read moves it to documented.' This finding is that page read, and it supplies the three things that record lacked. First, the form's own words confirming the two conditions it cited, read at first party. Second, a throughput figure grounded in a published index rather than in a tracker: 1,082 grantees across 53 main cohorts, 15 India cohorts, 116 countries, 2018 to 2026, from an independent atlas that states it compiled every published cohort announcement, with the announcement channel being the director's own blog. Third, the failure mode, which the existing record notes but does not name as the first thing that breaks. The record now reads: credentials are explicitly not weighed ('We probably don't care much about your formal education, credentials, or awards'), so the gate is the written proposal and one condition specific to this moment: the programme states it tests submissions and rejects AI-written ones, so an applicant who drafts the narrative with a model and does not rewrite it fails on detection rather than on merit. That is a mechanical statement of the programme's own published rule, not a judgement about it. A further feature worth recording: the form asks 'what is one mainstream or consensus view that you absolutely agree with', which is a written test of independent thinking rather than a test of credentials. What remains unestablished: the amount distribution (the existing record's 'USD 1k to USD 50k typical' is attributed to third-party trackers and is not on any operator page read today), the acceptance rate (no applicant count is published), and the payout rail for a non-US individual. Routes tried for those: the operator page, the application form, the atlas and two searches; no page states an applicant count.
